new_content.title: Listening and Attention
new_content.intro: This lesson is about listening and attention. Listening to a read-aloud, staying focused, and answering simple questions about what was heard. Work through the examples, then answer the questions at the end.

sections.heading: Listening and Attention
sections.body: Listening to a read-aloud, staying focused, and answering simple questions about what was heard.

sections.heading: An example, worked through
sections.body: "ch" in "chip" makes the ch sound, and removing it leaves "ip", which is a different word.
sections.example:
Which two letters make the first sound in "chip"?
Answer: ch

sections.heading: One step harder
sections.body: "ur" makes the vowel say er, which is why "turn" is spelled that way.
sections.example:
In "turn", the letter r changes the vowel to which sound?
Answer: er

check_questions.prompt: What does the prefix "dis-" mean in "disagree"?
check_questions.rationale: "dis-" means not, or the opposite of, so "disagree" is "agree" not, or the opposite of.

check_questions.prompt: In "play", which letters work together to make the long a sound?
check_questions.rationale: "ay" makes the long a sound in "play".

check_questions.prompt: In "tree", which letters work together to make the long e sound?
check_questions.rationale: "ee" makes the long e sound in "tree".
